rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Suspected measles cases require prompt collection of clinical and exposure details and public-health notification.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Measles response includes assessing close contacts and the risk of onward transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Measles is highly contagious and spreads more readily where vaccine uptake is low.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Two scheduled doses of MMRV provide very high protection against measles and rubella.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: People with measles can be infectious before the rash appears and for several days afterwards.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: UKHSA surveillance tracks laboratory-confirmed measles cases and regional and age distributions.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Healthcare and education settings need risk assessment, communication and infection-control action after suspected cases.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Checking vaccination status before international travel reduces the risk of infection and importation.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Measles risk depends on immunity, exposure, setting, contact intensity, timing and vulnerability to complications.

rows.source: UKHSA measles prevention and response
rows.verified: Measles surveillance evidence is case-, region-, age-, reporting-period- and vaccination-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Meningococcal disease can cause meningitis or sepsis and requires urgent medical assessment.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Symptoms can occur in any order and may include fever, severe headache and a non-blanching rash.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Vaccination is the best available protection against several meningococcal serogroups.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Public-health management includes laboratory investigation, contact assessment, prophylaxis and cluster response.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: The 2026 time-limited MenB offer targets defined Year 13 and new higher- or further-education entrant cohorts.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Eligible people are offered two doses, with programme deadlines extending into March 2027.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Shared residential education settings can increase opportunities for meningococcal transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Young adults are important in meningococcal carriage and transmission dynamics.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Meningococcal risk depends on age, immunity, carriage, close contact, living setting, strain and response timing.

rows.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease and MenB vaccination
rows.verified: Meningococcal evidence is person-, strain-, contact-, setting- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
